changelog: Paraphrased C8 to be shorter and to add an explicit instruction preventing extremely short fragments from being left alone when enforcing cohesion (addresses verb–complement shift side-effect).
Inserted a new Core Principle after C8 prohibiting cuts inside numeric/measurement/time expressions (addresses the primary finding about splitting quantities).
Inserted a new Core Principle after C8 requiring multi-character named entities and transliterations remain contiguous (addresses the finding about splitting names and transliterations).
findings: The prompt underestimates the harm of cutting inside numeric/measurement/time expressions: splitting percentages, speeds, durations or numeral+unit sequences often creates contradiction or loses core quantity information.
The prompt allows cuts that split multi-character proper names or transliterations, which severs referents and causes contradictions or incoherent fragments.
When rules forbid verb–complement splits, the prompt sometimes repositions cuts in ways that isolate punctuation or single-character function words; that trade harms short-piece bins.

diagnosis.why: Adding explicit rules to keep numbers and multi-character names contiguous pushed the model to stop splitting amounts/names (small positive gains across bins), but the paraphrase of C8 about avoiding extremely short fragments was interpreted in a way that moved cuts earlier and produced isolated single-character pieces (e.g. splitting 你 / 的), which explains the harmful tail moves even though overall bins improved slightly.
diagnosis.lesson: When strengthening safety for numbers and names, make the ‘avoid extremely short fragments’ instruction precise so it does not encourage moving cuts earlier and creating isolated one-character fragments.
